editorial: We lived in the US rather than maintaining one clean tourist expense sheet, so there is no honest three-week total to quote.

The structural costs are obvious: hotels in headline cities, rental cars, fuel, domestic flights and national-park accommodation. Food can range from inexpensive immigrant neighbourhood meals to financially irresponsible tasting menus within the same block.
A three-week coast-to-coast US trip is not a budget holiday, especially if you insist on staying centrally in Los Angeles, San Francisco and New York.

alternatives.title: What if we had a bigger budget?
editorial: Spend it on location and time. Stay centrally in New York and San Francisco, inside or close to Yosemite, and buy domestic flights at times that don't destroy entire days.
If the budget is much bigger, add Hawaii as its own proper leg rather than a two-day trophy stop.

alternatives.title: What if we had a smaller budget?
editorial: California plus Vegas and the Grand Canyon makes a coherent western trip. New York, Washington and perhaps New England make a coherent eastern one. Crossing the continent is where flights, one-way rentals and duplicated logistics start eating the budget.
